issues.description: Field 'lectureName' is declared as type String in the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md: line 64) but the solution implementation declares the Lecture.lectureName field with type LectureName (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: line 6). This changes the attribute's type students are expected to implement and creates a mismatch between the specification and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent across artifacts. Either revert the solution to declare 'private String lectureName' (and remove or adapt LectureName class), or update the problem statement, UML and template to require a LectureName type (and document the new type in the task and constructor signature).

issues.description: The exercise text asks students to implement a constructor that initializes lectureName (expected as a String) followed by the integer attributes (see problem_statement.md lines 19-21). The solution's constructor signature uses LectureName as the first parameter (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: line 13), causing a mismatch between the constructor students will implement and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature with the specification: either change the solution constructor to accept a String for lectureName (public Lecture(String lectureName, int ...)), or update the problem statement/template/UML to require a LectureName parameter and describe that type and its API to students.

issues.description: In the solution, the field 'lectureName' is declared as LectureName (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: line 6) but the getter and setter are declared with String types: getLectureName() returns String (line 22) and setLectureName(String) accepts String (line 26). The getter returns the LectureName field and the setter assigns a String to the LectureName field, which will not compile and therefore makes the reference solution invalid.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the solution's internal type consistency: either change the field to 'private String lectureName' so the getter/setter signatures are correct, or change the getter/setter signatures to use LectureName (getLectureName(): LectureName, setLectureName(LectureName)) and update all usages accordingly. Ensure the solution compiles before using it as a reference.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to the lecture's name as a String attribute named 'lectureName' (problem_statement.md: line 64), but the solution introduces a distinct type 'LectureName' and uses it as the field type (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java: line 6) and defines a LectureName class (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/LectureName.java: line 3). This represents the same conceptual entity with different identifiers/representations across artifacts and may confuse students expecting a simple String attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the representation and naming of the lecture name across artifacts. Prefer using a String for lectureName to match the UML: change the Lecture field type to String, update constructor/getter/setter signatures, and remove or repurpose the LectureName class. If a dedicated LectureName type is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require LectureName and document its API.
